title: Active learning guides copper-alloy catalysts with improved acetate selectivity
summary: An active-learning workflow combined learned adsorption-energy prediction with first-principles calculations to nominate copper–silver and copper–palladium catalyst compositions. Both synthesized candidates showed higher acetate selectivity than the pure-copper comparator in laboratory carbon-monoxide electrolysis. The result concerns these measured catalysts and conditions; mechanistic interpretation additionally depends on computational modelling, and commercial performance is not established.
ai_technology: Random-forest and XGBoost adsorption-energy prediction; active learning with first-principles calculations

evidence.tested: Learned-model-nominated Cu/Ag(3:1) and Cu/Pd(2:1) candidates were synthesized, characterized and evaluated against pure Cu in a zero-gap CO electrolyzer. Both improved measured acetate selectivity.
evidence.unknown: The abstract and Results reverse the 47%/50% Faradaic-efficiency assignment between the two alloys; this record therefore does not assign those exact values or rank the alloys. It represents the final 2025 CO-electroreduction study, not an earlier differently titled CO2 preprint. Absolute first-public priority and full preprint-version equivalence are unestablished. Mechanistic predictions, global optimality, industrial lifetime and deployment are outside the represented finding.
evidence.ai_role: Starting from 55 simulated alloy systems and 76 descriptors, iterative learned adsorption-energy prediction and new DFT calculations refine candidate selection. Random forest is the initial model and XGBoost the final comparison winner; the workflow selects the two compositions subsequently tested.

source_review.scope: Full primary journal/PMC text: exact identity, active-learning Methods, alloy selection, synthesis characterization, experimental Results/Fig8 caption and numerical-conflict caveat. Fresh primary bibliographic/status metadata.
